rationale: The claim that epileptic seizures occur in <=2/8 individuals (<=25%) is directly supported by OMIM #620450 reviewing Janssen et al. (2022), which records that only two patients had febrile seizures (one of whom had a single afebrile seizure). However, the specific assertion that muscular hypotonia (HP:0001252) occurred in >=5/8 individuals (>=62.5%) in Table 1 cannot be independently verified from the available text excerpts of Janssen et al. (2022) or OMIM #620450 in the provided SOURCES block. Furthermore, using seizure absence as an exclusionary criterion is clinically precarious given the small cohort size (n=8).

evidence.text: OMIM entry 620450 cites Janssen et al. (2022) and reports that two patients had febrile seizures, including one who also had a single nonfebrile seizure, among the cohort of individuals with TAF4-related neurodevelopmental disorder.

source.title: 620450 - INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 73; MRD73
source.quote: Two patients had febrile seizures, including 1 who also had a single nonfebrile seizure.

evidence.text: The discovery study for T4NDD established de novo putative loss-of-function variants across eight individuals presenting with intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms, without establishing hypotonia frequency in the abstract text.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: We here present a cohort of eight individuals, each carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 and expressing phenotypes consistent with a neuro-developmental disorder (NDD).

conflicts: The provided SOURCES block confirms low seizure frequency (2/8) from OMIM #620450, but omits the full Table 1 text of Janssen et al. (2022) needed to confirm the exact numerator for muscular hypotonia (>=5/8).

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact tally and HPO frequency of muscular hypotonia (HP:0001252) versus other neuromuscular signs across all published TAF4-NDD individuals?
new_directions.rationale: Directly reviewing Table 1 and supplementary phenotype tables of Janssen et al. (2022) and subsequent cohorts is required to determine whether hypotonia is truly present in >=62.5% of cases.
